Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
8:11 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a text. You open any payments app, scan a code or pick a contact, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. There is no card to carry, no cash to count and no change to wait for.

It has also reached places cards never did. Small shops, tea stalls and vegetable sellers just need a printed QR code, not a machine. Since most people already have a phone and a bank account, there is little to set up, and one app can work with almost any bank.

Here are the three main reasons:

Free and fast: Most everyday payments between people and at shops cost nothing, and they arrive instantly, any time of day, even on holidays.
Simple and everywhere: One QR code or phone number works across apps and banks, from big stores to street vendors.
Feels safe: Every payment needs your PIN, you see the amount before you confirm, and your bank details stay hidden from the person you pay.

Together, these make UPI quicker than cash and easier than cards, so more people use it each year.

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
8:14 AM

Here's a relaxed 3-day Jaipur plan, with only a couple of big sights each day so your parents aren't rushed:

Day 1, Forts and palaces: Amber Fort early, before the crowds and heat. Take a short photo stop at Jal Mahal on the way back. After lunch, see the City Palace and Jantar Mantar, then rest at the hotel.
Day 2, Old city: Hawa Mahal in the morning light, then Albert Hall Museum. Have a long lunch, then browse Johari Bazaar or Bapu Bazaar for jewellery, textiles and sweets. End with dinner and a folk show at Chokhi Dhani.
Day 3, Temples and views: Govind Devji Temple for the morning aarti, then Birla Temple. Visit Nahargarh Fort for the sunset view, then head to the station or airport.

Late October is pleasant in Jaipur, so mornings and evenings are the best time for walking. Hire a car with a driver for all three days, as Amber and Nahargarh have steep approaches and many steps.

Which dates are they travelling, and do they have any trouble with stairs? I can then adjust the pace.
